description: sevdesk tag relations — the join records linking a tag to an Invoice, Voucher, Order or CreditNote. READ-ONLY by grounding, not by omission: /TagRelation declares exactly one operation (get, operationId `getTagRelations`); sevdesk documents no POST /TagRelation, no PUT/PATCH, no DELETE, and no /TagRelation/{id} route of any kind, so this endpoint has no path placeholder. A relation is never created directly — the Tag tag group states verbatim that 'the tag relation does not have to be created separately, as this is automatically created when a tag is created'. The only route that produces one is POST /Tag/Factory/create, a different locator that belongs to the sibling `tag` endpoint and is already authored there as that endpoint's insert; it is deliberately not duplicated here. DELETE /Tag/{tagId} deletes the tag, not the relation. Full refresh only: Model_TagCreateResponse carries no `update` field, and sevdesk's createAfter/createBefore/updateAfter/updateBefore filter families are documented only for Contact, Invoice, Order, Voucher and CreditNote queries — never for Tag/TagRelation — so `create` cannot back an incremental read and no replication block is authored. Records are wrapped in `objects`. GET /TagRelation declares no `parameters` block at all (contrast GET /Tag, which declares id and name), so the only bound inputs are the connector-wide limit/offset pagination params.

schema.description: GET /TagRelation response envelope. Records are wrapped in `objects`; a top-level `total` is added only when countAll=true, which this endpoint does not send.

items.description: One tag relation (Model_TagCreateResponse, spec title 'Tag model', objectName example 'TagRelation'). The model declares exactly these seven properties, in spec order. It carries NO top-level `required` array and marks no property `nullable: false`, so every field is optional on the wire and none is declared required here; `id`, `objectName` and `create` are readOnly (system-set).

id.description: Unique identifier of the tag relation record (system-set, readOnly). The spec's description reads 'Id of the tag', but this is the id of the TagRelation record itself; the related tag's own id sits at `tag.id`. Declared type:string; the numeric value is serialized as a JSON string on the wire (spec example '1').

objectName.description: Model name; always 'TagRelation'. Not declared as an enum in the spec, but its description pins the constant ('Internal object name which is "TagRelation".') — authored as an enum for consistency with the sibling sevdesk endpoints.

additionalInformation.description: Additional information on the tag relation. Declared type:string with `default: null` and no example, i.e. null unless set.

create.description: Date of tag creation (system-set, readOnly) — the only temporal field on this model. Declared type:string, format:date-time. This model ships no example for the field and the operation ships no response example; the canonical follows the connector-wide date-time ruling rather than a per-field sample. sevdesk's date-time wire shape is offset-bearing across its models (e.g. Model_CheckAccountResponse.create '2024-06-28T14:42:58+02:00'). Not usable as a replication cursor — no create-after/before filter is documented on this route.

tag.description: The tag information — relation object {id, objectName='Tag'}, both required by the nested schema (id declared string, example '1'). Kept opaque.

object.description: The document the tag is attached to — relation object {id, objectName}, both required by the nested schema. Its `objectName` is enumerated [Invoice, Voucher, Order, CreditNote] and its `id` is declared INTEGER (unlike every other id in this model, which is string); both facts live on nested properties, so the parent stays opaque.

sevClient.description: Client relation the record belongs to ({id, objectName='SevClient'}); filled automatically by sevdesk. Kept opaque.
